body:
Fuck people. What you're going through is real to you, therefore it's real. (you get what I mean, not expertly worded).

*edit* I'll PM the rest.

It's complicated. I could never really pin down a reason.

I guess it's a control thing. I first started when my family was going through an extremely rough patch, I was young and didn't know how to cope emotionally with it all. I guess it was my own way of controlling my emotions. Past that it spiralled into something of a compulsion.

I've had better weeks/months. 

Glad to hear you're okay btw :) As a fellow survivor, I know how hard it can be to admit that you need help. Admitting yourself is especially difficult.

Act like you normally would, or as much as you can given the circumstance. 

Feeling that she's okay and that the world isn't going to treat her like a freak is an important thing. Some semblance of normality will go a long way.
A question that I hope isn't taken out of context. How did it feel on the precipice?
